detailed_solution.markdown:

ee:2002:q26.title: GATE EE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 26
ee:2002:q26.question:
A two port network, shown in figure is described by the following equations
$I_1=Y_{11}E_1+Y_{12}E_2$
$I_2=Y_{21}E_1+Y_{22}E_2$

The admittance parameters $Y_{11}, Y_{12},Y_{21},Y_{22}$ for the network shown are
options: 0.5 mho, 1 mho, 2 mho and 1 mho respectively
1/3 mho, -1/6 mho, -1/6 mho and 1/3 mho respectively
0.5 mho, 0.5 mho, 1.5 mho and 2 mho respectively
-2/5 mho, -3/7 mho, 3/7 mho and 2/5 mho respectively

primary.subtopicLabel: Two Port Network and Network Functions

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Two Port Network and Network Functions
detailed_solution.markdown:
Using KVL,

$E_1=2I_1+2(I_1+I_2)$

Again using KVL,

$E_2=2I_2+2(I_1+I_2)$

$$\Rightarrow \;\; [z]=\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2\\ 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$$

$[y]=[z]^{-1}$

$$\;\;=\frac{1}{(4 \times 4 )-(2 \times 2)}\begin{bmatrix} 4 & -2\\ -2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$$

$$\begin{bmatrix} Y_{11} & Y_{12}\\ Y_{21} & Y_{22} \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1/3 & -1/6\\ -1/6 & 1/3 \end{bmatrix}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ee:2002:q27.title: GATE EE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 27
ee:2002:q27.question: In the circuit shown in figure, what value of C will cause a unity power factor at the ac source?

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Resonance and Locus Diagrams
detailed_solution.markdown:
$Y=j\omega C+\frac{1}{30\angle 40^{\circ}}$

$\;\;=j\omega C+0.0255-j0.0214$

$\;\;=0.0255+j(\omega C-0.0214)$

$\;\;=Real(Y)+k Img(Y)$

To have unity power factor at ac source i.e. resonance condition,

$Img(Y)=0$

$\Rightarrow \;\omega C-0.0214=0$

$\because \; \omega =2 \pi \times 50$

$\therefore \; C=\frac{0.0214}{100 \pi}=68.1\mu F$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2002:q28.title: GATE EE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 28
ee:2002:q28.question:
A first order, low pass filter is given with R=50 $\Omega$ and C=$5\mu F$. What is the
frequency at which the gain of the voltage transfer function of the filter is 0.25?

primary.subtopicLabel: Magnetically Coupled Circuits, Network Topology and Filters

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Magnetically Coupled Circuits, Network Topology and Filters
detailed_solution.markdown: $T.F.=\frac{V_o}{V_i}=\frac{\frac{1}{j\omega C}}{R+\frac{1}{j\omega C}}$ $\;\;\;=\frac{1}{1+j\omega CR}$ $\therefore \; \; |Gain|=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+(\omega CR)^2}}$ $\;\;0.25=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+(\omega \times 5 \times 10^{-6} \times 50)^2}}$ On solving, $\omega =15.49 \times 10^3 r/s$ $\Rightarrow \;\; f=\frac{15.49}{2 \pi}=2.46 kHz$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ee:2002:q29.title: GATE EE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 29
ee:2002:q29.question: A series R-L-C circuit has R=$50\Omega$, L=$100\mu$ and C=$1\mu$. The lower half power frequency of the circuit is

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Resonance and Locus Diagrams
detailed_solution.markdown:
$\omega _0=\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$

$\;\;=\frac{1}{\sqrt{100 \times 10^{-6} \times 10^{-6}}}=10^5 r/s$

$\Delta \omega =\frac{R}{L}=\frac{50}{100 \times 10^{-6}}$

$\;\;=50 \times 10^4 r/s$

$\omega _{lower}=\left [ \sqrt{\omega _0^2+\left ( \frac{\Delta \omega }{2} \right )^2}- \frac{\Delta \omega }{2}\right ]$

$\;\;=\left [ \sqrt{(10^5)^2+\left ( \frac{5 \times 10^5}{2} \right )^2}-\frac{5 \times 10^5}{2} \right ]$

$\;\;=10^5\left [ \sqrt{1+6.25}-2.5 \right ]$

$\;\;=0.193 \times 10^5 r/s$

Hence, $f_{lower}=\frac{\omega _{lower}}{2 \pi}$

$\;\;=\frac{0.193 \times 10^5}{2 \pi}$

$\;\;=3065 Hz\approx 3.055kHz$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ee:2002:q44.title: GATE EE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 44
ee:2002:q44.question:
The transfer function of the system described by $\frac{d^{2}y}{dt^{2}}+\frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{du}{dt}+2u$ with u as
input and y as output is

detailed_solution.concept: Control Systems - Mathematical Models of Physical Systems
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\frac{d^2y}{dt^2}+\frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{du}{dt}+2u$$

$\Rightarrow s^2Y(s)+sY(s)=sU(s)+2U(s)$

$\therefore \;\; \frac{Y(s)}{U(s)}=\frac{s+2}{(s^2+s)}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2002:q45.title: GATE EE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 45
ee:2002:q45.question: For the system $$\dot{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0\\ 0&4 \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix} u; y=\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}X$$, with u as unit impulse and with zero initial state, the output, y, becomes

detailed_solution.markdown:
$x(t)=e^{At}X(0)+\int_{0}^{t}e^{A(t-\tau) }BU(\tau )d\tau$

$\because \;\; X(0)=0$  (as given)

$$\therefore \;\; x(t)=0+\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2(t-\tau )} &0 \\ 0 & e^{4(t-\tau )} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\delta (t)dt$$

$$\;\;=\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2(t-\tau )}\\ e^{2(t-\tau )} \end{bmatrix}\delta (t)dt$$

$$\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} e^{2t}\\ e^{4t} \end{bmatrix}$$

Output  $$y(t)=\begin{bmatrix} 4 &0 \end{bmatrix}x(t)$$

$$\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} 4 &0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2t}\\ e^{4t} \end{bmatrix}$$

Hence, $y(t)=4e^{2t}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ee:2002:q47.question: In the chopper circuit shown in figure, the input dc voltage has a constant value $V_{s}$. The output voltage $V_{o}$ is assumed ripple-free. The switch S is operated with a switching time period T and a duty ratio D. what is the value of D at the boundary of continuous and discontinuous conduction of the inductor current $i_L$?

detailed_solution.markdown: As the given chopper is buck chopper. $$\begin{aligned} V_0&=\alpha V_s\\ \Delta I&=\frac{V_0T_{off}}{L}=\frac{\alpha V_s(1-\alpha )}{Lf}\\ \Delta I&=2I_L=2I_0\\ \Delta I&=2I_0=\frac{\alpha V_s(1-\alpha )}{Lf} \end{aligned}$$ $\frac{\Delta L}{2}=I_{L(avg)}=I_{0(avg)}$ this is applicable only at the boundary of continuous and discontinuous $$\begin{aligned} L_c &=\frac{\alpha V_s(1-\alpha )}{2I_0f} \\ L_c&=\frac{\alpha V_sR(1-\alpha )}{R2I_0f} \\ (\because & \text{ multiplying and dividing by R}) \\ L_c&=\frac{V_0 R(1-\alpha )}{RI_02f} \\ L_c&= \frac{I_0R(1-\alpha )}{I_02f}\\ L_c&=\frac{R(1-\alpha )}{2f} \\ \therefore &= \text{ Boundary value of duty cycle is,}\\ \frac{2fL}{R}&=1-\alpha \\ \alpha &= 1-\frac{2fL}{R}=1-\frac{2L}{RT} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.
